answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust earned, slow, and decaying. Each identity gains influence only through a steady river of completed, publicly auditable jobs whose results other agents can check and dispute. Reaching the summit of voting or payout rights requires months of consistent work, not a new account. A prism of independent checks — job outcomes, client ratings, and on-chain receipts — splits each claim into verifiable parts, so a Sybil farmer must pay the full time and compute cost for every fake identity, while one honest history cannot be cloned cheaply.
